_comment: Single source of truth, read by BOTH Terraform (jsondecode(file(...)) in the
observability module, for the dashboard's cost metric math) and Python
(src/costs.py, for the README cost table and local estimates). An earlier
instinct was to put them in Terraform variables and repeat them in config.py;
duplicated constants that must agree are the same rot that made three
wildcard counts go stale in this repo.
EstimatedCostPerDocument is computed as CloudWatch metric math over real
emitted token counts times these numbers — not as a guessed per-document
figure. That is why they have to be data rather than prose.
Prices change. `retrieved` is the date to re-check, and the dashboard renders
it so a reader knows how stale the cost panel is.

bedrock._note: Per-token pricing is model-specific. Changing bedrock_model_id in tfvars without updating these makes the cost panel wrong while still looking plausible — which is worse than a blank panel. There is a test asserting the two agree.

textract._note: DetectDocumentText, first 1M pages/month tier. AnalyzeDocument is ~15-65x more expensive per page, which is why the OCR state uses DetectDocumentText.

sagemaker._note: The endpoint's standing cost. Billed per instance-hour whether or not it serves traffic, which is why it dominates a mostly-idle graded run and why deploy_endpoint defaults to false.

stepfunctions._note: STANDARD workflow state transitions. This intake workflow is ~14 transitions per auto-approved document, so ~$0.00035/document — negligible next to Textract and Bedrock, which is worth knowing before optimising the state count.

cloudwatch._note: The dashboard fee is per dashboard per month beyond the first three. Custom metrics are charged per metric name x dimension combination, which is the reason the metric set is dimensioned by environment and document_class only — adding correlation_id as a dimension would create one metric per document and is the classic way to turn a $3 dashboard into a four-figure bill.
